newsitem.title: GERMANY: German workers strike as allied troops seek cuts.
newsitem.headline: German workers strike as allied troops seek cuts.

text.p: Civilians employed by allied troops in Germany, already facing heavy post-Cold War job cuts, will stage protests against new cost-cutting measures by their military employers, a German trade union said on Wednesday.

Staff at about 20 American, British and French bases in Germany are to organise work stoppages to protest against measures that threaten the jobs of the 35,000 civilians still employed at the bases, Germany's OeTV public sector union said.

The union said in a statement that the move followed the break-down of negotiations with military leaders stationed in Germany last month over compensation to workers whose jobs are at risk because of cutbacks.
"We tried to agree a social plan offering protection to employees but this has been rejected," a spokeswoman for the OeTV union said.

The union estimated that some 65,000 civilian jobs in Germany have already been scheduled to go as a result of the reduction in the foreign troop presence that has followed the warming of relations with the ex-Soviet Union.
The troop pull-out has also had a devastating effect on the economies of a number of small German towns that relied heavily on spending by troops at local bases.
The OeTV said British and U.S. bases in particular were now seeking to reduce their costs further through rationalisation measures.

A statement issued on Wednesday by the U.S. army European command in Heidelberg said it proposed to unions last month that employees adversely affected by the cost-cutting be offered higher severence payments, an offer which was turned down.
